newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crude action slim, Latam demand perks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crude action slim, Latam demand perks.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude business was thin Thursday, but regional trading moves were seen in the Latin American sector, traders said.
Chilean state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) bought a cargo each of Angolan Palanca and Ecuadorian Oriente in its latest purchase tender for December.
Traders said ENAP bought one million barrels of Palanca laoding at the end of November, and 400,000 barrels of Oriente for early December loading.
Elf sold the Palanca at Dated Brent plus 25 cents a barrel fob, and Oriente was dealt by Glencore at an unknown price.
Uruaguay's state oil refiner ANCAP said it was seeking 600,000 barrels for December delivery, reduced from normal levels due to a planned shutdown at the La Teja refinery.
For North Sea dealings to the U.S., the arbitrage remained restrictive, but margins in Europe were called "favorable," leading to business there.
Supplies remained plentiful, however, and paper Brent was hit by the unbalanced fundamentals.
There was one confirmed wet Brent trade seen.
Traders said a November 15-17 loader was sold at December Brent minus 54 cents, three cts firmer than the previous Dated deal seen Wednesday.
In the U.S. aftermarket, traders said a pair of full paper Brent cargoes were sold.
One parcel switched hands at $22.35 a barrel, 10 cts firmer that the IPE December settlement, but the second full cargo was sold at $22.27.
A partial trade was heard at $22.28, and two December/January spreads were done at plus 27 cts and 28 cts.
